props.title: Operation Thunderbolt

sections.content: Operation Thunderbolt stands as a pivotal moment in Israeli action cinema, dramatizing the real-life 1976 IDF rescue mission at Entebbe Airport. The film blazed a trail for other military operation thrillers like Delta Force (1986) and Zero Dark Thirty (2012). Director Menahem Golan crafted a taut, documentary-style approach that influenced later hostage rescue films like Raid on Entebbe (1976) and 7 Days in Entebbe (2018). The film's success helped establish Golan-Globus as a major force in 1980s action cinema.

sections.content: The film pioneered several techniques that became standard in military operation thrillers. Like Black Sunday (1977) and Munich (2005), it blends actual news footage with dramatized sequences. The parallel editing between hostages, terrorists, and rescue planners created a template followed by films like Argo (2012) and Captain Phillips (2013). Its emphasis on operational details and military precision influenced countless special forces films. SUBHEAD: Impact on Military Action Cinema

Operation Thunderbolt helped establish conventions for depicting special forces operations that echo through modern cinema. Its influence can be seen in everything from Navy SEALs (1990) to Zero Dark Thirty (2012). The film's commitment to authenticity - using actual Israeli military personnel as advisors and filming at similar locations - set a standard for military accuracy that later films like Black Hawk Down (2001) would follow. Its success also paved the way for other Israeli military films like Beaufort (2007) and Lebanon (2009).
